author: Lena Martinez
content:
Overview

This playbook is a consolidated sales enablement resource for Redwood Inference covering positioning & messaging, competitive brief guidance, pitch deck outlines, pricing guidance, representative case studies, and a security FAQ designed for prospect conversations. Use this document as the single-source-of-truth for go-to-market teams and field sellers.

Audience and use cases
- AEs and SDRs preparing discovery and demo narratives.
- Solutions engineers and SEs building technical validation and POCs.
- Product marketing creating pitch materials and one-pagers.
- Customer-facing leaders preparing for procurement and security reviews.

Owner and maintenance
- Primary owner: Go-to-market (RevOps / Product Marketing).
- Technical reviewer: Eng Serving Runtime.
- Review cadence: Quarterly or after major product/price changes.

1) Positioning & Messaging

Elevator pitch (30 seconds)
Redwood Inference is the developer-first inference platform that makes LLM-powered applications predictable and economical at scale. We deliver consistent latency, transparent unit economics, and flexible deployment (hosted, dedicated, private) so engineering teams can ship faster without building and operating custom inference stacks.

Three core value props (for different buyer personas)
- Engineering/Platform teams: Unified runtime and API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments; reduces operational burden and fragmentation.
- Product teams/PMs: Predictable latency and cost controls (batching, caching, quantization) that preserve user experience while lowering unit cost.
- Security/Compliance stakeholders: Private deployment options, KMS integrations, and audit logging to meet enterprise security requirements.

Message playbook by stage
- Discovery: Focus on SLAs (latency/uptime), model catalog flexibility, and predictable pricing. Ask: "What are your latency SLOs and peak tokens/sec?"
- Demo/POC: Highlight quick onboarding, example SDK calls, and live perf numbers. Show a model swap and a canary rollout in the console.
- Procurement: Emphasize contract types (reserved capacity for Dedicated, enterprise licensing for Private), data residency, and support SLAs.

2) Competitive Briefs (how to use and a short matrix)

Competitive messaging approach
- Always lead with customer problem and value (e.g., "You need predictable cost and SLA-backed latency for a high-concurrency chat product").
- Use differences in operational burden and deployment flexibility as primary differentiators.
- Avoid product feature-dump; focus on economics (tokens/second, cost per 1M tokens), fallbacks, and observability.

Example competitor comparison table (summary)
| Competitor | Deployment modes | Strengths | Typical weak points vs Redwood |
|-----------|------------------|----------|-------------------------------|
| Public LLM API A | Hosted only | Large model catalog, simple pricing | No private deployment, limited SLA options |
| Cloud Provider B | Hosted + VM endpoints | Deep infra integration | Higher ops customization required, inconsistent docs |
| Self-hosted Runtime C | Private only | Full control | High ops burden, lacks managed fallbacks and observability |
| Redwood Inference | Hosted / Dedicated / Private | Unified API, predictable economics, rollout tooling | Newer than incumbents in some regions (mitigations: partners & dedicated capacity) |

Competitive rebuttals (short scripts)
- "We can self-host to reduce cost:" Acknowledge control but highlight total cost of ownership: engineering time, fragmentation across teams, and lack of unified rollout/traceability.
- "We can use provider X because it’s cheaper:" Ask for real workload numbers; show how batching, KV caching, and quantization recommendations typically reduce unit costs by 20–60% in production compared to naive endpoints.

3) Pitch Deck Guidance and Slide Outline

Recommended 10–12 slide deck structure for an initial enterprise pitch
1. Title + one-line positioning (use elevator pitch)
2. Customer problem & impact (quantify: p50 latency, conversion lift, cost leakage)
3. How Redwood solves it (three pillars: performance, economics, deployment choice)
4. Product demo screenshots (console routes, model catalog, rollouts)
5. Serving architecture at a high level (runtime, kernel selection, smart routing)
6. Observability & ops (dashboards, token-level cost)
7. Pricing models (summary table)
8. Case study (metrics and ROI)
9. Security & compliance (highlight SOC2, KMS, audit logs)
10. Implementation plan & timelines (POC -> Pilot -> Production)
11. Pricing ask / commercials
12. Next steps & ask

Pitch best practices
- Use one metric-driven story per deck (latency, cost, or reliability).
- Include a two-slide appendix for technical deep-dive (runtime internals, network/topology, model compatibility).
- Bring an SE for technical discovery when the deck is first shared.

4) Pricing Guidance (rep-level guidance; not legal pricing)

Pricing primitives
- Hosted API: usage-based (tokens per request & embeddings) with free tier/credits. Best for fast POCs and small-scale production.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU capacity for predictable throughput. Monthly/annual commitments, configurable autoscaling policies.
- Private: enterprise licensing and support for on-prem or VPC deployments. Typically includes platform fee + deployment/maintenance fees.

Representative pricing table (example ranges; use ops-approved sheet for final numbers)
| Model of engagement | Billing basis | When to recommend | Example commercial levers |
|----------------------|---------------|--------------------|---------------------------|
| Hosted (self-serve) | Per-token + per-embedding | Early-stage customers, dev/test | Rate limits, tiered discounts |
| Dedicated (reserved) | Committed monthly GPU units + overage | Production systems with predictable throughput | Burst packs, autoscale policy levels |
| Private (enterprise) | Platform fee + support + deployment | Regulated workloads, on-prem | KMS/HSM integration charges, compliance add-ons |

Guidance for pricing conversations
- Discovery: collect expected QPS, peak tokens/second, SLA needs, and data residency. Use these to recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
- POC -> Pilot: recommend Hosted for speed unless data residency or performance predictability requires Dedicated.
- Negotiation: trade term length and commitment for price breaks and preferential capacity.

5) Case Studies (short, copyable templates)

Case study template (one-paragraph summary + bullets)
- Customer: [industry, company size]
- Use case: [e.g., conversational support, code generation, search rerank]
- Challenge: [e.g., high latency, unpredictable costs, compliance] 
- Solution: [hosted/dedicated/private + key features used (batching, quantization, KV cache, routing policies)]
- Outcome: [metrics: latency p95 reduced from X->Y, cost per 1M tokens down Z%, uptime/SLA improvement] 

Example case: Conversational support (SaaS)
- Customer: FinServ startup (Series B, ~120 employees)
- Use case: Real-time chat assistant for customers handling KYC/resolution flows.
- Challenge: p95 latency spiking to 1.2s during peak usage and opaque token spend.
- Solution: Deployed Redwood Dedicated with autoscale policy, KV prefix caching, and model quantization profile recommended by Redwood Optimize.
- Outcome: p95 latency down to 380ms, steady throughput of 450 requests/sec, estimated 42% reduction in token spend vs prior endpoint, SLA-backed uptime for production.

Sales-ready one-liner (copyable)
- "We helped [customer] reduce p95 latency by 70% while cutting inference spend by ~40% through dedicated capacity combined with caching and quantization."

6) Security FAQ for Prospects (concise answers reps can share)

Q: Where is customer data stored and how do you support data residency?
A: Redwood supports region-specific deployments for hosted and Dedicated customers; Private deployments allow full on-prem/VPC control. We provide documentation for region availability and data residency options during procurement.

Q: Do you support customer-managed keys?
A: Yes. We integrate with KMS/HSM providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, customer HSM) for private key management in Private and Dedicated configurations.

Q: Is traffic/encryption in transit and at rest?
A: All customer traffic is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2/1.3). Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256 and optionally using customer-managed keys where supported.

Q: What compliance certifications do you hold?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II. We provide a compliance packet on request; specific enterprise evidence and questionnaires (e.g., ISO, HIPAA) are handled via our security & compliance team and may require a Private deployment and an executed DPA.

Q: How do you handle model outputs that might leak PII?
A: We provide configurable data retention and redaction policies, monitoring for anomalous outputs, and recommend local model filters and prompts for redaction in sensitive flows. For regulated workloads, we recommend Private deployments with no persistent storage of raw requests by default.

Q: Do you support audit logging and traceability?
A: Yes. Audit logs are available for Dedicated and Private customers and include request metadata, model/version used, timestamps, and operator actions. Logs can be exported to customer SIEMs or S3/GCS buckets.

Q: What is your incident response process for security events?
A: Our security incident response follows documented runbooks: triage, containment, customer notification timeline (initial ack within 24 hours), and a post-incident analysis. Contact security@redwood-inference.internal for escalation.

Q: Can we run Redwood in an air-gapped environment?
A: Yes — Private on-prem packaging supports air-gapped deployments; additional professional services engage for installation, validation, and audit.

7) Sales Playbook: Step-by-step for an AE + SE pair
1. Pre-call: Review customer token/QPS estimates, compliance needs, and likely deployment preference.
2. Discovery call: Validate SLOs, dataset sensitivity, latency requirements, and procurement constraints.
3. Technical workshop (with SE): Run a small perf test or demo using a representative prompt set. Collect p50/p95 latencies and token counts.
4. Recommend engagement model: Hosted for rapid POC, Dedicated for throughput predictability, Private for compliance.
5. Commercial proposal: Use pricing primitives, propose pilot period (30–90 days) with measurement gates.
6. Pilot success criteria: Latency target, cost target, error rate reduction, and operational readiness.
7. Production rollout: Plan canary rollout using console rollouts and automated fallback policy.

Appendix: Technical reference snippets (copy-paste for SEs)
- Example SDK call (Python)
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="<key>")
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-1-large", prompt="Summarize the following text...", max_tokens=150)
print(resp.text)
```

- Example rollout CLI snippet
```
redwood rollouts create --model redwood-1-large --route production --canary 10% --fallback-model redwood-1-fast
```
